name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_SEQUENCING_Q01 - Extinction threat percentage across major taxa

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following taxonomic groups in ascending order based on the percentage of their species currently facing the threat of extinction worldwide according to the IUCN:

(I) Mammals
(II) Birds
(III) Amphibians
(IV) Gymnosperms

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The question requires ordering four major taxonomic groups (Mammals, Birds, Amphibians, and Gymnosperms) in ascending order (lowest percentage to highest percentage) according to the proportion of their species facing global extinction threat documented by the IUCN.

Step 2: Identify the documented extinction threat percentage for each taxon
According to the IUCN Red List statistics presented in the textbook:
- Birds: 12 percent of all bird species face the threat of extinction.
- Mammals: 23 percent of all mammal species face the threat of extinction.
- Gymnosperms: 31 percent of all gymnosperm species face the threat of extinction.
- Amphibians: 32 percent of all amphibian species face the threat of extinction.

Step 3: Compare and arrange in ascending order
Comparing the numerical threat values:
12 percent (Birds) < 23 percent (Mammals) < 31 percent (Gymnosperms) < 32 percent (Amphibians).

Step 4: Formulate the sequence
Replacing each taxon with its respective numeral yields the sequence: (II) followed by (I), then (IV), and finally (III).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Birds exhibit the lowest vulnerability among the four groups at 12 percent, whereas amphibians exhibit the highest vulnerability at 32 percent, confirming that the proper ascending order is Birds → Mammals → Gymnosperms → Amphibians, corresponding to the sequence (II) → (I) → (IV) → (III).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIODIVERSITY_AND_CONSERVATION_SEQUENCING_Q02 - Chronological sequence of global biodiversity milestones

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following international environmental summits, reports, and target commitments in the correct chronological sequence (from earliest to latest):

(I) The historic Convention on Biological Diversity ('The Earth Summit') held in Rio de Janeiro
(II) Release of the IUCN Red List documenting the extinction of 784 species over the preceding 500 years
(III) The World Summit on Sustainable Development held in Johannesburg, South Africa
(IV) Target year committed by 190 countries to achieve a significant reduction in the rate of biodiversity loss

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The task requires arranging four major global conservation milestones and commitments described in the chapter in chronological order from earliest to latest based on their documented calendar years.

Step 2: Determine the calendar year for each milestone
- The Earth Summit (Convention on Biological Diversity) in Rio de Janeiro was held in the year 1992.
- The World Summit on Sustainable Development in Johannesburg, South Africa, took place ten years later in the year 2002.
- The publication of the IUCN Red List documenting 784 recent extinctions was released in the year 2004.
- During the Johannesburg summit in 2002, 190 participating nations pledged their commitment to achieve a significant reduction in biodiversity loss by the target year 2010.

Step 3: Arrange the events chronologically
Ordering by calendar year:
1992 (The Earth Summit) → 2002 (World Summit in Johannesburg) → 2004 (IUCN Red List 2004) → 2010 (Pledged commitment target year).

Step 4: Formulate the sequence
Associating each date with its designated numeral yields the progression: (I) in 1992, followed by (III) in 2002, then (II) in 2004, and concluding with (IV) in 2010.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verifying the chronological timeline confirms that the Earth Summit occurred first (1992), followed by the Johannesburg Summit (2002), the IUCN Red List publication (2004), and the pledged target year (2010). Thus, the correct sequence is (I) → (III) → (II) → (IV).
